title: Flatshiftcars Track Pack 1: UK & Navarra
intro:
[h1]Flatshiftcars Track Pack 1: UK & Navarra[/h1]
Eight circuits you've driven, or always wanted to, rebuilt for Wreckfest from real survey data. The crests that go light, the cambers that hold you in, the braking boards where you know you should've braked. Seven from Britain, one from northern Spain: {circuits} circuits, {layouts} layouts.

[b]No noise limits. No black flags for drifting. No queue for the pit exit.[/b]

[b]Standalone and stable.[/b] No other mods, packs or asset libraries needed: subscribe and race. Every circuit runs hundreds of automated checks before it ships, so it loads first time and won't crash your game, unlike most of the track mods out there.

Every corner sits where it does in real life. The racing line comes from OpenStreetMap, the hills and camber from laser-scanned ground models, and the track width is measured metre by metre, then checked against real lap data from an AiM dash. Kerbs, gravel, Armco and tyre walls are where the real ones are. On top: a 24-car grid, AI drivers, a minimap and the real start lights.

Follow [b]@flatshiftcars[/b] on Instagram for track days and builds.
lapNote: Lap lengths are as built in the game.
usage: Subscribe, then enable [b]Flatshiftcars Track Pack 1: UK & Navarra[/b] in the Mods menu and restart the game. Each layout is an event, e.g. "Brands Hatch Indy".
Online: the server and every player need the mod enabled (server: copy the mod folder into the server's mods folder and add that folder's name to mods= in server_config.cfg).
Don't enable it together with separate single-circuit versions of these tracks: the same track in two mods clashes.
changeNote: Renamed to Flatshiftcars Track Pack 1: UK & Navarra. AI brakes properly for tight corners; smooth junctions (no humps, gaps or grass); bridge banners flush; no flickering grandstands or pit walls; better TV cameras on hills; checkpoints on every shortcut; Anglesey Coastal start line; Bedford Turn 7 corrected; new sponsors (TEAMYAG, Trackstormers, SeriouslyLotus).

blurbs.brandshatch: Paddock Hill Bend. You crest the brow blind, the road falls away beneath you, and the car goes light just as you need it most. Then up the hill to Druids, the hairpin that's caused more first-lap pile-ups than anywhere in Kent. Take the GP loop and you're out into the woods: Hawthorn, Westfield and Dingle Dell at proper speed, with nowhere to hide.
blurbs.oultonpark: England's prettiest circuit is also one of its most savage. Old Hall, then the plunge through Cascades and down past the lake. Knickerbrook, then the climb to Clay Hill, where the car lifts right at the top. Brittens and Hislop's are there to slow you down; the cones on the Trackday layout show you where to go.
blurbs.cadwellpark: The "Mini Nürburgring", tucked away in the Lincolnshire Wolds. Narrow, twisting and never level. The Mountain is where bikes take off, and in a Wreckfest banger you will too. Thread the Gooseneck, dance through Hall Bends, and stay off the grass: it's closer than it looks.
blurbs.doningtonpark: Turn in at Redgate, then let it fall away through the Craner Curves, one of the best sequences of corners anywhere, all commitment and no visibility. The Old Hairpin, Starkey's, McLeans and Coppice, then down the straight to the Melbourne Hairpin, a late-braking contest every single lap.
blurbs.snetterton: A Norfolk airfield turned proper racetrack. Flat, fast and harder than it looks. The Bentley Straight goes on forever, so the brakes take the punishment, and the 300's infield will catch out anyone who thinks flat means easy.
blurbs.anglesey: Racing on the edge of Wales, literally: the sea is right there. Big skies, crosswinds and the Corkscrew dropping towards the water. Four layouts, from the flowing International to the tight little Club.
blurbs.bedfordautodrome: A sprawling airfield with run-off you could land a plane on. That's handy, because you'll use it. Four layouts, from the long GT lap to the tight West circuit: made for side-by-side battles and learning where the limit is.
blurbs.navarra: Northern Spain, under big skies with mountains on the horizon. A modern, flowing circuit with long, fast sweepers and heavy braking zones, and three layouts to pick from, including the 2024 extension.
